title: Cognitive Development and Language Acquisition in Indonesian Early Childhood:
text_snippet: Cognitive Development and Language Acquisition in Indonesian Early Childhood: Language acquisition during early childhood is closely associated with cognitive development and shaped through meaningful social interaction. However, empirical evidence explaining how cognitive development influences language acquisition in authentic Indonesian kindergarten classrooms remains limited. This study explored the relationship between cognitive development and language acquisition among Indonesian early childhood learners through naturally occurring classroom interactions. A qualitative multiple-case study involved 30 children aged 4–6 years from four kindergartens in Sukoharjo Regency, Central Java, Indonesia. Conducted from January to March 2026, data were collected through classroom observations, semi-structured teacher interviews, and document analysis and analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, supported by triangulation and member checking. The findings revealed two major themes. title: Teachers' Strategies for Addressing Reading Delays through Multisensory Learning:
text_snippet: Teachers' Strategies for Addressing Reading Delays through Multisensory Learning: Reading is a foundational skill that determines students' academic success, yet many elementary school students in Indonesia still experience reading delays. It aims to explore teachers' strategies in overcoming reading delays through multisensory learning at SD Negeri Bendo. A qualitative case study approach was employed, with data collected through in-depth interviews, participant observation, and documentation. The subjects were three lower-grade teachers and the school principal, selected purposively. Data were analyzed using Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña's interactive analysis model, with data validity ensured through source and technique triangulation. The findings reveal six key aspects of teachers' strategies: (1) planning through VAKT-based teaching modules tailored to students' characteristics; (2) implementation integrating visual, auditory, kinesthetic, and tactile activities in a sequential learning cycle; (3) supporting factors including school policy support, learning facilities, parental collaboration, and teacher professional commitment; (4) inhibiting factors dominated by students' heterogeneous reading abilities, time constraints, lack of structured implementation

title: Digital Technology Integration in Elementary English Language Teaching:
text_snippet: Digital Technology Integration in Elementary English Language Teaching: The integration of digital technology in English Language Teaching (ELT) has changed the teaching and learning process, but its successful integration in elementary schools is highly dependent on teachers’ familiarity with technology and pedagogical digital literacy. This qualitative multi-site case study aimed to investigate how three elementary school English teachers in Wonosobo, Indonesia, integrate digital technology into their ELT classrooms by examining their instructional practices, implementation procedures, student engagement patterns, and challenges encountered. The data were collected through classroom observations and semi-structured interviews with three teachers from three different elementary schools. Thematic analysis revealed that teachers used PowerPoint, Youtube, Quizizz, Google Forms, Canva, and digital storytelling applications adopting scaffolding pedagogical approaches. Technology integration positively affected students’ behavioral, emotional and cognitive engagement, which led to increased motivation, participation and vocabulary retention. title: Effects of Limited Language Exposure on Oral Fluency
text_snippet: Effects of Limited Language Exposure on Oral Fluency In this study, the researcher investigated how limited language exposure affects oral fluency and, ultimately, learners’ participation in English First Additional Language (EFAL) classrooms. The study was grounded in Stephen Krashen’s (1985) input hypothesis, which emphasizes the importance of language exposure for improving oral fluency. Data were collected qualitatively through focus group interviews, semi-structured interviews, and non-participant observation with the eight Grade 10 EFAL learners and two EFAL teachers at a selected school in the Sekgosese East Circuit, Mopani East District, Limpopo Province, South Africa. The study found that, in the context where the school is situated, learners have limited language exposure due to the dominance of Sepedi outside the classroom and little exposure to English. The study further found that the school is under-resourced and, as a result, there are few materials to support fluency development. Observed learner disengagement was found to result from learners’ poor articulation. title: Politeness Strategy Retention as a Mechanism of Pragmatic Equivalence in the Indonesian Translation of Macbeth
text_snippet: Politeness Strategy Retention as a Mechanism of Pragmatic Equivalence in the Indonesian Translation of Macbeth Literary drama translation requires translators to preserve not only semantic meaning but also the pragmatic construction of characterization. While previous studies have predominantly examined shifts in politeness strategies across languages, the role of strategy retention as a mechanism for preserving pragmatic equivalence has received little scholarly attention. This study investigates how retained politeness strategies function to preserve characterization in the Indonesian translation of Shakespeare’s Macbeth. Using a qualitative descriptive design, the study analyzes 92 utterances from Act 1 in which politeness super-strategies are retained from the source text to the target text. The findings demonstrate that translators systematically retain bald-on-record, positive politeness, and negative politeness strategies when these strategies encode socially significant meanings, including monarchical authority, in-group solidarity, and manipulative intimacy. Rather than reflecting a failure to adapt to the target culture, such retention functions as a deliberate mechanism for preserving pragmatic equivalence while maintaining the original characterization and dramatic tension. title: Exploring Student Speaking Competence Through Role-Based Differentiated Assessment in Project-Based EFL Learning
text_snippet: Exploring Student Speaking Competence Through Role-Based Differentiated Assessment in Project-Based EFL Learning Differentiated assessment has been proposed to accommodate students’ diverse roles and abilities in collaborative speaking activities. However, speaking instruction in many EFL classrooms still relies on memorized dialogues and uniform assessment, limiting fairness and authentic evaluation of communicative competence. Moreover, few studies have integrated Project-Based Learning (PjBL) and differentiated assessment into a role-based speaking assessment framework from students’ perspectives. This study explored the implementation of role-based differentiated speaking assessment in PjBL, students’ speaking performance across communicative roles, their perceptions of the assessment process, and its challenges and benefits. A qualitative case study was conducted with ten senior high school students in an English Club Program in West Java. Data were collected through classroom observations, semi-structured interviews, and document analysis, then analyzed using thematic analysis with data triangulation. title: Amplifying Voices: Enhancing EFL Speaking through Video-Based Assessment
text_snippet: Amplifying Voices: Enhancing EFL Speaking through Video-Based Assessment Speaking is a fundamental skill in English language learning, yet many students face various challenges in developing it effectively. To address these issues, several strategies can be implemented, one of which is video-based assessment. This study investigates the impact of video-based assessment on students’ speaking performance and explores their responses to its implementation. A qualitative research design was employed, involving the use of video-based tasks and interviews with participants. The assessment procedure followed step-by-step guidelines adapted from Dal (2010), based on the Task-Based Learning framework proposed by Willis (1996). The participants were 11th-grade high school students. The results showed that nearly all students experienced improvements in their speaking scores from the first to the third video submission. An increase was also observed in the class average score. In addition, score classification using Harris’s (1974) criteria indicated a shift from lower to higher performance categories. title: Apperception as a Communication Event to Foster Mindful Learning in Indonesian Language Learning
text_snippet: Apperception as a Communication Event to Foster Mindful Learning in Indonesian Language Learning Apperception is commonly viewed as an introductory learning activity that connects students’ prior knowledge with new material. However, existing research still tends to treat apperception merely as a procedural step and has not sufficiently examined its role as a communicative event that fosters mindful learning. This study aims to describe apperception as a communicative event that promotes mindful learning in Indonesian language instruction. This study employed a qualitative approach using Dell Hymes’s ethnography of communication. It was conducted in Class VIII E at SMPN 2 Kalinyamatan, involving an Indonesian language teacher and students. Data were collected through non-participant observation, semi-structured interviews, documentation, and field notes, and analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, interpreted through Hymes’ SPEAKING components. The findings show that apperception functions as a communicative event constructed through the interrelationships of Setting and Scene, Participants, Ends, Act Sequence, Key, Instrumentalities, Norms, and Genre. title: Reconceptualizing Kurikulum Berbasis Cinta: English Teachers' Cognition and Classroom Implementation
text_snippet: Reconceptualizing Kurikulum Berbasis Cinta: English Teachers' Cognition and Classroom Implementation Kurikulum Berbasis Cinta (KBC) has recently been introduced by the Indonesian Ministry of Religious Affairs as a value-oriented curriculum promoting empathy, respect, compassion, and meaningful relationships in education. Although previous studies have examined KBC from the perspectives of character education and classroom implementation, limited attention has been given to how English teachers interpret its principles and translate them into English language teaching. This study explored English teachers' cognition of KBC, its classroom implementation, and the challenges encountered during practice. Employing a qualitative descriptive design, the study involved four English teachers from two Madrasah Tsanawiyah (MTs) in Cilacap Regency, Indonesia. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, classroom observations, and lesson plan analysis and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed that teachers perceived KBC as an educational approach integrating character development with English language teaching through supportive teacher–student relationships, collaborative learning, and meaningful classroom interaction. title: Teacher’s Perception of Video-Based Learning in ELT for ASD Students in Inclusive Classroom
text_snippet: Teacher’s Perception of Video-Based Learning in ELT for ASD Students in Inclusive Classroom The integration of video-based learning has become increasingly common in inclusive English Language Teaching (ELT) classrooms as educators seek effective strategies to support students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). This study explored an English teacher’s perceptions of the use of video-based learning for students with autism in an inclusive classroom. Employing a qualitative case study design, the research involved an English teacher at an inclusive senior high school in North Sumatra, Indonesia. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, classroom observations, and teacher reflective journals and were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed that video-based learning played an important role in supporting students’ emotional regulation, sustaining attention, and encouraging participation during classroom activities. Students demonstrated greater enthusiasm and engagement when exposed to visual and auditory content. However, a significant engagement–comprehension gap was identified. title: The Implementation of Wayground for Speaking Activities and Students’ Responses in an Inclusive Junior High School EFL Classroom
text_snippet: The Implementation of Wayground for Speaking Activities and Students’ Responses in an Inclusive Junior High School EFL Classroom This study aimed to investigate the implementation of Wayground (formerly known as Quizizz) as a game-based learning platform to support speaking activities in an inclusive EFL classroom and to explore students’ responses toward its use. This study employed a descriptive qualitative research design. Data were collected through classroom observations, semi-structured interviews with the teacher and students, and documentation. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s (2006) framework. The findings revealed that Wayground was implemented through teacher-guided speaking activities in which questions were displayed via a projector and students were encouraged to respond orally in English. The findings also indicated that students demonstrated active participation in speaking activities and classroom interactions during the implementation of Wayground. In addition, students perceived the learning activities as engaging and enjoyable, which encouraged participation among learners with different levels of speaking ability and self-confidence. title: Developing a Genre-Based ESP English Module for Vocational Accounting Students
text_snippet: Developing a Genre-Based ESP English Module for Vocational Accounting Students Preparing vocational students for workplace communication has become an important objective of English language education. However, English instruction for vocational accounting students remains predominantly based on general English materials that inadequately address their workplace communication needs. Although previous studies have investigated English for Specific Purposes (ESP), Genre-Based pedagogy, or instructional material development, few have integrated these components into a systematic instructional framework for vocational accounting education. This Research and Development (R&D) study aimed to identify vocational accounting students’ English language needs, develop an ESP-based English module through a Genre-Based Approach, and evaluate the validity, practicality, and effectiveness. The study adopted the ADDIE instructional design model and involved 30 Grade XI Accounting and Financial Institution students at a vocational high school in Indonesia. title: The Place of Artificial Intelligence in the Communicative Approach:
text_snippet: The Place of Artificial Intelligence in the Communicative Approach: The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), in language education is frequently discussed in terms of effectiveness alone. This article offers a theoretically grounded critical evaluation based on key principles of the Communicative Approach, including authentic communication, communicative competence, interaction, production, willingness to communicate, affective dimensions, socioculturally mediated communication, and critical pedagogy. It argues that LLMs create new opportunities for implementing communicative language teaching by expanding interaction, feedback, learner output, and access to language resources. However, these technologies simultaneously constrain the fundamental aims of the communicative approach because they only simulate, rather than genuinely embody, the social, intersubjective, and intentional dimensions of communicative competence. These limitations are therefore structural rather than incidental. Accordingly, the article neither promotes uncritical technological optimism nor rejects educational technology altogether. title: English for Specific Purposes in the Digital Era:
text_snippet: English for Specific Purposes in the Digital Era: This study examines the relevance of English for Specific Purposes (ESP) in the digital era by integrating needs analysis, AI literacy, and work readiness among students of the Faculty of Teacher Training and Education at Ekasakti University. The study is motivated by the increasing demand for prospective teachers to possess not only general English proficiency, but also academic, professional, digital, and AI-supported communication skills. A mixed-method approach was employed, involving questionnaires, interviews, and document analysis to identify students’ English learning needs, their awareness and use of AI tools, and their readiness to enter the teaching profession. The findings indicate that students need more contextual ESP materials related to educational terminology, academic reading, classroom communication, teaching material development, professional presentation, and digital communication. The study also reveals that AI literacy plays an important role in supporting students’ English learning, particularly in improving writing, enriching vocabulary, understanding academic texts, preparing presentations, and developing learning resources. title: Teachers’ Perspective on the Implementation of Merdeka and K-12 English Curricula
text_snippet: Teachers’ Perspective on the Implementation of Merdeka and K-12 English Curricula English language curriculum reform has become increasingly important in Southeast Asia as countries seek to enhance learners’ communicative competence and global competitiveness. Although studies have been done on Indonesia’s Merdeka Curriculum and the K to 12 Curriculum of the Philippines, most studies have examined these curricula separately, and the focus has mostly been on policy formulation rather than curriculum implementation. This article attempts to fill this gap by exploring the implementation of these two curricula particularly in terms of learning objectives, content, pedagogy, and assessment from the teachers’ perspectives. Using a qualitative comparative case study design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 10 secondary English teachers from the Philippines and Indonesia (five teachers from each country), questionnaires, and document analysis. Thematic analysis indicated that both curricula promote communicative competence and develop learners’ macro language skills. title: Exploring Teacher Educators’ Self-Assessment of AI-Assisted Writing:
text_snippet: Exploring Teacher Educators’ Self-Assessment of AI-Assisted Writing: This study attempts to explore how English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teacher educators perceive the impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted writing on their academic writing practices, with a focus on self-assessment. Using a qualitative case study, semi-structured interviews were conducted with six early-career lecturers from universities in Eastern Indonesia who actively use AI-assisted writing tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, and QuillBot. The findings show that AI enhances linguistic accuracy, coherence, writing efficiency, and confidence by providing immediate feedback and supporting independent revision. At the same time, participants expressed concerns about overreliance, creativity loss, and authorship, leading them to regulate AI use critically and reflectively. The findings also highlight contextual challenges related to institutional support, digital infrastructure, and unequal access to AI resources, alongside expectations for more integrated AI applications. title: Exploring Eighth Grade Students’ Anxiety in Learning English at SMPN 2 Bolo
text_snippet: Exploring Eighth Grade Students’ Anxiety in Learning English at SMPN 2 Bolo Foreign Language Anxiety (FLA) is one of the psychological factors that may influence students’ performance in learning English as a Foreign Language (EFL). Although anxiety is commonly associated with students who have low language proficiency, it can also be experienced by students with relatively good English ability. From a psycholinguistic perspective, anxiety may interfere with cognitive processes involved in language learning, such as attention, memory, and language production. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the types of foreign language anxiety and the factors contributing to anxiety among eighth-grade students with relatively good English proficiency at SMPN 2 Bolo. This study employed a descriptive qualitative design with a psycholinguistic approach. Four participants were selected through purposive sampling based on predetermined criteria, including high academic achievement, relatively better English proficiency, teacher recommendation, and observable indications of anxiety during classroom interaction, particularly speaking activities. title: The Author’s Worldview in the Novel Teruslah Bodoh Jangan Pintar by Tere Liye
text_snippet: The Author’s Worldview in the Novel Teruslah Bodoh Jangan Pintar by Tere Liye This research aims to describe the author's worldview in the novel "Teruslah Bodoh Jangan Pintar" by Tere Liye, particularly as reflected in the themes, characters, plot, and conflicts, based on Lucien Goldmann's theory of genetic structuralism. This study employs a qualitative approach, specifically literary sociology. The data obtained consist of words, phrases, quotations, and sentences that are interrelated with the author's worldview. Data were collected using observation and note-taking methods, and analyzed using Lucien Goldmann's dialectical method. The results of the study explain the author's worldview, which is realized through the themes, characters, plot, and conflicts. This worldview is used to express various ideologies, ideas, values of life, and criticisms of the realities of life within the scope of society. Several phrases used in the novel require attention to the politeness culture that has been reflected in Indonesian society. Furthermore, this research proves that the use of sarcasm in the novel "Teruslah Bodoh Jangan Pintar" by Tere Liye can influence readers' understanding of the meanings conveyed in the novel, both explicitly and implicitly.

title: Sociocultural Perspective on Teaching Critical Listening through Music in English First Additional Language Classroom
text_snippet: Sociocultural Perspective on Teaching Critical Listening through Music in English First Additional Language Classroom This study explored how music can facilitate the teaching of critical listening in English First Additional Language (EFAL) classrooms from a sociocultural perspective. Grounded in sociocultural theory, the study examined how music-mediated listening activities support learners’ development of critical listening skills through social interaction, cultural mediation, and collaborative learning (Maniraj, 2026; Nakanishi, 2025). A systematic qualitative review research design was adopted to synthesise evidence from previous studies, theoretical literature, and scholarly discussions on the integration of music in language teaching. The review analysis shows how music serves as a cultural and pedagogical tool that promotes learners’ ability to interpret, analyse, evaluate, and discuss spoken and musical texts critically. Furthermore, the study identified effective pedagogical practices that EFAL teachers can employ to foster critical listening through music-based activities. title: An Investigation of Teachers’ Roles in Implementing Project-Based Learning in Elementary Education
text_snippet: An Investigation of Teachers’ Roles in Implementing Project-Based Learning in Elementary Education Understanding the right way to effectively implement Project-Based Learning (PBL) in classroom situations while overcoming challenges such as student engagement in the classroom might be a huge issue for teachers. This research explores the experiences, perceptions, and challenges of an elementary school teacher implementing Project-Based Learning (PBL) in their classroom. Using a qualitative approach within the framework of Vygotsky’s theory on socio-cultural, the study focuses on one teacher selected through purposive sampling based on their experience with PBL. Data collection involves semi-structured interviews to understand the teacher’s strategies, challenges, and perceptions. The findings reveal that teachers perceive themselves primarily as facilitators, emphasizing their role in creating a supportive learning environment that fosters student engagement and enhances learning outcomes. While the study highlights the positive impacts of PBL on student collaboration and critical thinking, it also identifies potential obstacles, such as time management and diverse student needs. title: Exploring Students’ Engagement in Learning Comparison through AI-Assisted Canva Games
text_snippet: Exploring Students’ Engagement in Learning Comparison through AI-Assisted Canva Games The integration of technology in education has expanded rapidly, including the use of digital learning media to create more interactive and enjoyable learning experiences. One of these media is Canva, which has become a popular educational design platform. The novelty of this study lies in the use of Canva AI features to develop interactive learning media and create simple educational games more efficiently. This study aimed to explore student engagement in learning comparison through the use of AI-Assisted Canva Games. The research was motivated by students’ low interest and participation in conventional classroom learning. A descriptive qualitative method was employed, with data collected through observations, interviews, and documentation. The participants were 13 fifth-grade students from an elementary school in Simalungun Regency, North Sumatra, who participated in English learning using AI-Assisted Canva Games. The participants were selected purposively because they were directly involved in the implementation of the learning media. title: Understanding Student Engagement and Writing Skills through Interactive Game Based Activities among Young Learners in EFL Classrooms
text_snippet: Understanding Student Engagement and Writing Skills through Interactive Game Based Activities among Young Learners in EFL Classrooms This study explores the relationship between student engagement and writing skills through interactive game-based activities in an elementary EFL classroom. Elementary students often display varying levels of participation and experience difficulties expressing their ideas in English, both orally and in writing. While previous studies have primarily emphasized learning outcomes, this research focuses on students’ engagement during interactive activities and their responses to writing tasks in a game-based learning environment. A qualitative case study design was employed involving 11 sixth-grade students from a public elementary school in Simalungun Regency. Data were collected through classroom observations, semi-structured interviews, and documentation, then analyzed interpretively to examine students’ behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement in writing activities and their learning experiences. journal_name: International Journal of Language Teaching and Education
title: Challenges and Strategies of a Private English Tutor in Teaching Autistic Children:
text_snippet: Challenges and Strategies of a Private English Tutor in Teaching Autistic Children: Private English tutoring for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) has received little attention in the field of inclusive education, even though its role is becoming increasingly relevant as a supportive alternative to formal schooling. This study aims to identify the challenges and strategies of a private English tutor in teaching children with ASD using an intrinsic qualitative case study approach, with data collected through semi-structured interviews, observations, and document analysis. The findings indicate that communication difficulties, a preference for routines, repetitive behaviors, and context-inappropriate behaviors each present challenges that the tutor must address independently without institutional support. In response, the tutor developed strategies such as visual aids, student-interest-based materials, structured routines, real-time instructional adjustments, and positive reinforcement. This study underscores the need for inclusive teacher training programs that reflect the realities of teaching English to students with ASD outside formal institutions.

title: Between Help and Hesitation:
text_snippet: Between Help and Hesitation: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into higher education, creating new opportunities for academic writing, research, and learning support. However, concerns regarding academic integrity, source reliability, and responsible AI use remain significant, particularly among future educators. This study explores how English Language Teaching (ELT) graduate students engage with AI tools in their academic practices. A qualitative approach was employed involving open-ended questionnaires completed by 13 ELT graduate students, followed by semi-structured interviews with five participants and reflective written responses from four participants. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed three major themes: AI as Linguistic and Cognitive Scaffolding, negotiating trust, verification, and academic integrity, and emerging professional beliefs about responsible AI use. Participants perceived AI as a valuable resource for idea generation, academic writing, language development, and conceptual understanding. title: Language Proficiency, Information Behavior, and Reliance on Official Information among BIPA Learners
text_snippet: Language Proficiency, Information Behavior, and Reliance on Official Information among BIPA Learners This study explored the relationship between Indonesian language proficiency and information behavior patterns, specifically reliance on official information sources, among BIPA learners in Indonesia. Using an explanatory quantitative design, data were collected through an online survey from 92 respondents (prior and currently enrolled in BIPA programs from multiple universities in Indonesia). The instrument captured language proficiency, patterns of electronic resources use, perceived accessibility, and reliance on official information channels. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability testing, correlation analysis, and multiple regression using IBM SPSS Statistics 31. The findings indicate that while language proficiency is positively associated in reliance, it does not significantly predict reliance when controlling for passive accessibility. Instead, passive accessibility emerges as the strongest predictor. The research findings show that BIPA learners interact with the digital information environment, relying moderately on official information channels. title: Between Informal Engagement and Classroom Passivity:
text_snippet: Between Informal Engagement and Classroom Passivity: This study explores the challenges influencing students’ investment in Indonesian Islamic boarding schools (pesantren), and how students negotiate these challenges. Drawing on Darvin and Norton’s (2015) model of investment, it examines qualitative data from focus group discussions with 29 students and semi-structured interviews with three English teachers from three pesantren schools in West Java. The findings reveal a discrepancy between learners’ high informal engagement with English and their limited classroom participation, which cannot be explained simply by low motivation or limited proficiency. In this context, learners’ investment is influenced by institutional regulations, pedagogical constraints, examination priorities, and moral discourses that frame English as both opportunity and ethical risk. Some cases show how learners may remain highly invested in English while strategically limiting their classroom participation when existing forms of engagement did not align with their aspirations or values. title: Reflective Practice in EFL Teacher Professional Development:
text_snippet: Reflective Practice in EFL Teacher Professional Development: This study investigates the role of reflective practice in empowering English language teachers toward sustained professional development. Despite its recognized importance, many in service teachers struggle to integrate reflective routines into their daily practice due to systemic and personal constraints. Using a qualitative design, data were collected from eight postgraduate English education students at Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia through open-ended questionnaires. Responses were analysed using Braun and Clarke’s (2006) thematic analysis framework. Findings reveal five interconnected barriers: time constraints arising from heavy institutional workloads, limited access to reflective resources and tools, insufficient collaborative culture within schools, methodological uncertainty in selecting appropriate reflection strategies, and sceptical attitudes toward the value of reflection. These challenges are contextually shaped by individual, institutional, and cultural factors. title: AI Tools in Academic Writing: Indonesian EFL Students' Perspective
text_snippet: AI Tools in Academic Writing: Indonesian EFL Students' Perspective The purpose of this study was to explore Indonesian EFL students’ beliefs and challenges regarding the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in academic English writing. A mixed-methods approach was employed, involving a descriptive survey of 112 students from the English Education Department at Universitas Muhammadiyah Purwokerto and semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data provided an overview of students’ AI usage patterns, while qualitative data offered deeper insights into their experiences and perceptions. The findings revealed that students generally held positive attitudes toward AI tools and used them for idea generation, grammar checking, vocabulary enhancement, and text organisation. AI tools were also perceived to increase confidence and reduce writing anxiety, supporting both cognitive and affective aspects of learning. However, participants expressed concerns about overreliance on AI, the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated content, issues of originality, and academic integrity. title: Digital Literacy and Academic Writing in the Age of AI:
text_snippet: Digital Literacy and Academic Writing in the Age of AI: In today’s AI-mediated educational landscape, digital literacy is a crucial skill for language learners and educators. This study investigates the relationship between digital literacy competence and academic writing performance among EFL undergraduate students. Employing a sequential explanatory mixed-method design, the study involved 68 sixth and eighth-semester students who had completed ICT and academic writing courses. Data were collected through a Digital Literacy Scale (DLS) questionnaire, an online academic writing test monitored using AI-based auto-proctoring tools, and follow-up interviews. Results showed that while most participants demonstrated high digital literacy, there was no statistically significant correlation between composite digital literacy scores and academic writing performance. title: Investigating Students’ Levels and Challenges in Promoting Autonomous Learning:
text_snippet: Investigating Students’ Levels and Challenges in Promoting Autonomous Learning: Over the past three decades, autonomous learning has emerged as a hot topic in language learning. This study investigates the learner autonomy levels and the challenges faced by English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners in an Indonesian university context. Using a qualitative method, data were collected through a structured survey with 30 participants and follow-up interviews with four graduate students. The survey is based on Bandaranaike & Willison’s framework. The results were analyzed using thematic analysis by Braun & Clarke (2006). Results revealed that learners showed moderate autonomy, confidence in guided tasks, critical thinking, but faced challenges in initiating independent tasks, managing time, planning objectives, managing communication, and relying on teacher guidance. Future research could investigate more on the ICT application in enhancing students’ autonomous learning.

title: Representations of Sexual Violence in Islamic Boarding Schools on Nu. or.id and Mubadalah.id:
text_snippet: Representations of Sexual Violence in Islamic Boarding Schools on Nu. or.id and Mubadalah.id: Islamic boarding schools (pesantren) across two Indonesian online news outlets: NU Online and Mubadalah.id. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the study integrates Fairclough's three-dimensional Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) framework, transitivity analysis within Halliday and Matthiessen's Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL), and corpus-assisted discourse analysis using the SketchEngine platform. The data corpus comprises 25 articles from NU Online and 18 articles from Mubadalah.id published between 2022 and 2025, all addressing cases of sexual violence within pesantren environments. The findings reveal that, despite both outlets being rooted in the organisational tradition of the Islamic mass organisation Nahdlatul Ulama, they construct markedly divergent discursive representations of sexual violence. title: Internal and External Reform of Javanese Language in Deli Javanese Dialect in Binjai City: A Phonological and Lexicon Study
text_snippet: Internal and External Reform of Javanese Language in Deli Javanese Dialect in Binjai City: A Phonological and Lexicon Study The Javanese language of the Deli dialect in Binjai City developed in a multilingual situation that brought Javanese speakers together with Indonesian, Deli Malay, and other language elements in everyday communication. This study aims to describe the forms of internal and external renewal of the Javanese language of the Deli dialect in Binjai City, especially in the aspects of phonology and lexicon. The study used a diachronic linguistic approach with a qualitative descriptive method. Data in the form of lingual units showing sound changes, changes in form, and vocabulary replacement were collected through the listening method and the conversation method with the techniques of tapping, noting, recording, fishing, speaking semuka, and vocabularies. Analysis was carried out through the classification of phonological and lexical changes, determination of retention and innovation, and the principles of lexicostatistics and dialectometry. title: Making Notes for Teaching Reading: The Implementation of Reading to Learn Program (R2L) in an EFL Classroom
text_snippet: Making Notes for Teaching Reading: The Implementation of Reading to Learn Program (R2L) in an EFL Classroom This paper investigates the implementation of note making from the Reading to Learn (R2L) program where students make notes from their reading texts and at the same time learn to read. R2L is known to support literacy development but one specific phase, note making during the Joint Construction stage particularly in Indonesian EFL classrooms, remains largely unreported. This case study examines how the note making phase serves as a learning scaffold to teach reading. The study employs a pedagogic register to analyze classroom interactions and teacher-student relationships. The data were drawn from the classroom interaction recordings during the Joint Construction stage of R2L instruction. The findings indicate that pedagogical interaction during note making was characterized by explicit instruction, guided participation, affirmative scaffolding, and collaborative engagement between teacher and students. title: Development of Android-Based Learning Media SiBudiman for Biography Text Material in Class X Students
text_snippet: Development of Android-Based Learning Media SiBudiman for Biography Text Material in Class X Students Educational technology advancement demands learning methodologies aligned with interactive, autonomous ecosystems. This research developed SiBudiman, an Android-based learning media employing hybrid architecture (MIT App Inventor frontend + Google Sites backend cloud storage) for Biography Text instruction (Merdeka Curriculum Phase E, Grade X). The hybrid design produced a lightweight application (≤10 MB) with rich multimedia content, representing a methodological innovation addressing storage limitations while maintaining content quality, a critical gap in literature where prior offline Android applications consumed 50-100 MB. Using 4D model (Define, Design, Develop, Disseminate), expert validation encompassed content, language, and media dimensions. Quasi-experimental pre-post control group design tested effectiveness (n=33 experimental, n=30 control). Validation achieved 86.7% average (content 90%, language 90%, media 80%), with iterative revision addressing identified media design improvements. title: Pedagogical Scaffolding and Cohesive Writing in English First Additional Language Classroom: The Qualitative Case Study of Grade 9 Teaching Practices in Rural Secondary School
text_snippet: Pedagogical Scaffolding and Cohesive Writing in English First Additional Language Classroom: The Qualitative Case Study of Grade 9 Teaching Practices in Rural Secondary School This study examined the pedagogical practices employed in teaching essay writing to Grade 9 English First Additional Language (EFAL) learners in a rural Limpopo school, analysing the relationship between these practices and learners' use of cohesive devices in written composition. Drawing on non-participant observations of six one-hour lessons, semi-structured interviews with two EFAL teachers, and systematic document analysis of 10 learner essays using a cohesive devices analytical framework, the study investigated how instructional approaches shape learners' capacity to produce coherent, cohesive texts. The findings indicate that both observed teachers predominantly employed teacher-centred, product-oriented approaches that emphasised grammatical accuracy and structural replication over the recursive processes of planning, drafting, and revising. title: EFL Students’ Functional and Cognitive Dependency on ChatGPT in EFL Academic Writing
text_snippet: EFL Students’ Functional and Cognitive Dependency on ChatGPT in EFL Academic Writing The increasing use of ChatGPT in academic writing has raised concerns about students' dependency on artificial intelligence, particularly in EFL contexts. This study examines students' functional and cognitive dependency on ChatGPT as theoretically distinct constructs and describes dependency patterns across gender. A descriptive quantitative design was employed involving ten fourth-semester English Education students at STKIP Taman Siswa Bima. Data were collected through a questionnaire (functional: α = .830; cognitive: α = .632) and self-reflection responses analysed thematically, with findings triangulated to strengthen credibility. The results revealed higher functional dependency (M = 3.66) than cognitive dependency (M = 3.29). Students primarily relied on ChatGPT for grammar correction, vocabulary improvement, sentence construction, and paraphrasing, while cognitive support was associated with idea generation and argument development. Thematic analysis yielded three themes: reasons for use, perceived benefits, and awareness of over-reliance. Gender differences were minimal. title: Navigating Barriers: Teachers’ Perspectives on Implementing TBLT to Develop EFL Speaking Skills
text_snippet: Navigating Barriers: Teachers’ Perspectives on Implementing TBLT to Develop EFL Speaking Skills Task-Based Language Teaching (TBLT) has become a widely advocated approach to developing English speaking competence in EFL classrooms due to its interactive and communicative nature. Nevertheless, its implementation in practice is often influenced by various factors that may undermine its effectiveness. This study aims to explore the challenges faced by the teachers while implementing TBLT to teach speaking and the solutions they employ to deal with these challenges. To achieve this objective, a qualitative approach was used, involving 11 English teachers from secondary schools who were purposely selected based on their experience in employing TBLT in their classrooms. Using a thematic analysis of qualitative data collected from open-ended questionnaires, the study categorizes findings into two major themes: the obstacles encountered in practical application and the possible solutions suggested. title: Bringing Stories to Life: Investigating the Role of Stories in Young EFL Learners’ Reading Comprehension
text_snippet: Bringing Stories to Life: Investigating the Role of Stories in Young EFL Learners’ Reading Comprehension Young EFL learners, especially in Indonesia, often encounter challenges in reading comprehension due to linguistic limitations and cultural unfamiliarity, which can hinder both understanding and motivation. Although reading comprehension is emphasized in the national curriculum, the need for more effective and contextually relevant instructional strategies remains pressing. This study explores the role of stories in supporting young EFL learners’ reading comprehension. Employing a qualitative approach, data were collected through open-ended questionnaires and semi-structured interviews with 10 primary school English teachers in Indonesia. The findings reveal that each stage of the narrative genre contributes uniquely to reading comprehension. Orientation supports literal understanding through vocabulary exposure and contextual clarity; complication fosters inferential thinking by enabling prediction and causal reasoning; and resolution along with re-orientation promote critical comprehension through reflection on character actions and moral lessons.
